clearedSpotChecks.check: What a wrong register or spill decision of the gcc-built emitter could do to a mined block, and whether mined history already rules it out on the paths it has used (tracing nodes run InterpreterOnly, block policy rejects a proposal whose delayed execution header differs).
clearedSpotChecks.note: I fetched https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.7/cmd/monad/main.cpp and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad-bft/v0.16.7/monad-eth-block-policy/src/lib.rs and they are byte-identical to the unit's copies. main.cpp:485-488 selects vm::VM::InterpreterOnly when trace_calls is set and Dual otherwise. lib.rs:1181-1195 rejects a block with ExecutionResultMismatch when its execution results differ from the node's own, and lib.rs:1276-1295 takes those results from the block execution_delay sequence numbers back. I queried rpc.monad.xyz myself: web3_clientVersion returns Monad/0.16.7, and block 0x77e7c58 (125,729,880) returns hash 0x8799...6a51, state root 0x9eab...5cb1 and receipts root 0xc134...36e0, matching the unit's log. One link is inferred: that these endpoints serve callTracer because they execute with trace_calls, and so with the interpreter. The unit already limits the clearance to paths that mined transactions entered and leaves unentered PoolManager blocks open as a lead. With that scope the clearance holds.

clearedSpotChecks.check: SLOAD and SSTORE of the gcc 15.2.0 build at the mainnet revision (sload<MonadTraits<10>> at 0x450670, sstore<MonadTraits<10>> at 0x451fd0) against runtime/storage.cpp:36-121.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I read out/fn/0000000000451fd0.s against storage.cpp:56-104. The static flag test at Context+0x20 exits with status 2. The test gas_remaining + remaining_block_base_gas <= 0x898 (2200) equals the source's test against 2300 with min_gas 100. Cold access charges 0x1f40 = 8000. The charge after update_page is worked out as follows: cmp al,1 then sbb gives -1 when first_page_write is 0, which is masked to -2800. neg rax and a 32-bit and with 0x4268 give 17000 or 0, and the 32-bit and zero-extends. Adding 0xaf0 gives 2800a + 17000b, which equals 100 + 2800a + 17000b - 100. No refund write appears, which fits the MIP-8 branch, and traits.hpp:283-286 makes MIP-8 active from MONAD_TEN. The unit cited revision.h:35-39 as proof that mainnet runs MONAD_TEN, but those lines are only the enum. The proof is in https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.7/category/execution/monad/chain/monad_mainnet.cpp:30-31 (MONAD_TEN from timestamp 1788359400), which I fetched, and in the latest block on rpc.monad.xyz (125,738,549 with timestamp 1795745479), which I queried. Running normdiff.py again gives 76/76 instructions with 0 differences for sstore and 54/54 with 0 differences for sload between the revision 10 and 11 instances. The conclusion stands, and only the revision citation needs to change.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Whether cycle 28's reading of call_impl<MonadTraits<11>> at 0x42ed10 applies to call_impl<MonadTraits<10>> at 0x42e5d0, which mainnet runs (382 instructions, 0 differences after normalisation).
clearedSpotChecks.note: I reran scripts/normdiff.py on out/fn/000000000042e5d0.s and out/fn/000000000042ed10.s, and it prints len 382 382 differ 0. I also checked that the normalisation does not hide branch targets. The regex removes only the absolute address and the function name, and the in-function offset stays in the compared text. The first eight conditional-jump offsets (+0x590, +0x560, +0x590, +0x5d0, +0x590, +0x190, +0x6d0, +0x590) are equal in both listings. Rip-relative operands are compared by their resolved absolute target, so the two instances would differ if they read different constants. The identity holds, and cycle 28's call reading carries over to MONAD_TEN. The gas-forwarding test in the next cleared item ran on a clang harness and does not cover gcc native code. The unit states this, so it is no error.
